g.text: How context fills, where tokens go, and how to keep costs under control
Every byte that enters Claude's context window costs tokens — here is how a typical Claude Code session breaks down.
File reads / tool outputs — usually the biggest cost driver
Main Conversation — How it fills up
Each message grows the context. Heavy tool use accelerates it.
A summary replaces history — nuance and detail are lost
Automatic compaction preserves the gist but can lose critical detail: earlier decisions,
code context, error patterns. Run /compact proactively to control timing.
Sub-agents run in their own context. Only summaries return to the main thread.
Five high-impact strategies to reduce context consumption
Not all browser actions are equal. Choose the cheapest tool that validates your goal.
How quickly tokens add up in a typical session
Fixed per-session overhead — always present regardless of conversation length.
Stacks fast across sessions. 10 files = 40k tokens before any tool output.
per Read call, accumulated in history
Test suites, build logs, npm installs. Pipe to head or capture summaries.
Exact error messages, intermediate reasoning steps, prior file
contents, and nuance in earlier decisions are lost in summary.
Proactive /compact before critical work preserves what matters.
Token consumption patterns — Claude Code internal documentation
Context window: up to 200k tokens | Compaction threshold: ~85% fill | Sub-agent isolation: full separate context
